tools.name: rotate_model
tools.description: Orbit the camera around the model on screen. Positive yawDegrees moves the camera to the right around the model, negative to the left. Positive pitchDegrees moves the camera up to look down on it. The state's yawDegrees and pitchDegrees say where the camera is now.

yawDegrees.description: Degrees to orbit left or right, from -360 to 360.

pitchDegrees.description: Degrees to orbit up or down, from -80 to 80. Leave out to keep the height.

tools.name: zoom
tools.description: Move the camera closer to or farther from what it looks at. factor 1.3 moves about 30 percent closer, 0.7 about 30 percent farther. The state's zoom runs from 0 (farthest) to 1 (closest).

factor.description: Above 1 zooms in, below 1 zooms out, from 0.3 to 3.

tools.name: zoom_to_part
tools.description: Move the camera to one labeled part, make it glow, and dim the others. label must be one of the state's labels.

label.description: A label from the state's labels.

tools.name: reset_view
tools.description: Show the whole model again from the starting angle, with no part highlighted, assembled and closed.

tools.name: answer_with_screen
tools.description: Answer a question about what is on screen, using a screenshot. Use it for questions and for anything no other tool can do, not for changing the view.

tools.name: build_new_scene
tools.description: Build a brand new 3D model from scratch, which takes about 10 seconds. Use it only when the learner wants a different model or a 3D view of something not on screen yet, never to turn, zoom, or open the model already showing.

asQuiz.description: true when they asked to be quizzed or tested on it.

tools.name: pop_out
tools.description: Lift the subject of the video frame or the largest picture in Chrome's front tab out in 3D with its parts labeled. Use it when they say pop this out.

tools.name: close_scene
tools.description: Close the 3D scene on screen. A paused video plays again.

tools.name: explain_part
tools.description: Say what one labeled part does, while the camera turns to it. label must be one of the scene state's labels.
